Alright so heres what i want you to map out into a
  coherent idea for me, basically, we use to let you
  models/agents
      write code that would make 3d models, they fell
  extremely short. now we have a very capable studio
  editor for 3d
      modeling, and all the tools necessary. so what id
  like to see happen is to be able to open a session of
  claude or
      kimi or codex and be able to send an image or
  just a descriptive prompt, they would then be able to
  place a cube,
      make cuts, pull on edges, you know, all the
  things i would do by hand. ideally, it would be in
  real time, showing
      me what they are building, so that i can revert
  to a point where i can tell if they are messing up or
  something i
      dont like.  Pretty much a 'MCP' but dont use an
  actual mcp since its just going to end up being
  likely just some
      typescript api and a skill on how to use it.
  anyways, lets see what u can sauce up   and we might
  run with it
resolution: Mapped the ask into a coherent design and wrote it to docs/game/AGENT_SEAT_DESIGN.md (commit 0d90a72e8). No code changed. Surveyed the existing surface first and found the seat is mostly assembly, not new machinery: ModelToolApi already carries ~40 real verbs (extrudeFace, loopCut, bevel, weld, solidify, glass, detach, merge, pathArray), the mesh journal already holds labeled full snapshots plus __mesh_journal_checkpoint, __mesh_action_drain already streams accepted commits WITH source attribution, CommandAuthority's CommandSource already contains 'remote' and 'automation', /tmp/reactjit.sock already routes NOTICE JSON into the JS runtime, and __capture_frame already lets the app screenshot itself. The design names the real gap: every tool verb has the signature verb() — both the noun (which faces) and the amount (how far) come from the human's hand via viewport clicks and gizmo drags or a host-owned popup, which an agent cannot supply. The repo already solved this twice for tests (__mesh_gizmo_nudge/scale_by are documented as camera-free headless hooks), so the seat completes a pattern rather than inventing one. Five parts: a host-resolved selector language (facing:+y, part:roof, loop:, set algebra) so the agent never holds an index that a topology op will invalidate; parameterized ops that all bottom out in existing verbs; a cheap text percept plus on-demand ortho shots; takes (journal mark + thumbnail + staggered ~100ms application so the user actually watches it model) with rewind and a generation stamp that rejects in-flight ops after a rewind; and a seat policy with hold/step/take-the-wheel. Wire is a SEAT verb on the existing dev socket plus rjit seat CLI verbs, so any agent that can shell out can join — no MCP. Seven build slices, with the selector resolver as the load-bearing one. Risks called out, chief among them that a seat firing 40 ops in seconds is exactly the load that trips the derived-copy consistency matrix (req_3469-3486), making the stable-handle work a companion to slice 1 rather than unrelated.
